title: Current-mirror OTA
description: A current-mirror (or current-amplifier) OTA: the input pair drives diode-connected mirror loads, and each mirror is copied with ratio $K_m$ to a push-out output branch, so the effective output transconductance is $K_m*g_{m,in}$. This buys bandwidth and slew almost for free — GBW = $K_m*g_{m,in}/(2*\pi*C_L)$ and SR = $K_m*I_{tail}/C_L$ — but not DC gain: raising $K_m$ scales both the output transconductance and the output conductance together, so the low-frequency gain is nearly independent of $K_m$. The catch shows up in noise: to hit a fixed GBW at larger $K_m$ the input pair shrinks ($g_{m,in}$ falls as $1/K_m$), so its input-referred thermal density grows as $\sqrt{K_m}$. The current-mirror node carries a real pole; its estimate is shown but settling is sim-owned.

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the output mirror devices' vds

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input CM at which the operating point is evaluated

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: K_m
params.note: mirror ratio: multiplies GBW and SR, but raises input noise as sqrt(K_m) at fixed GBW

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise floor

params.name: gm_id_ml
params.note: input-mirror (diode) inversion: sets the mirror-node pole

params.name: gm_id_mo
params.note: output-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher output resistance

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs, used to place the tail node; retune until input-bias-consistent is green

params.name: vgs_est_ml
params.note: estimate of the input-mirror diode vgs, used as its own vds; retune until mirror-bias-consistent is green

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, driving the diode mirror load.

doc.title: Input mirror device (diode)
doc.description: Diode-connected mirror load at half the tail current; its vds equals its own vgs and its gate node carries the mirror pole.

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side)
doc.description: The K_m-scaled output copy carrying K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is one half of the output conductance and its gate cap loads the mirror node.

doc.title: Output mirror device (NMOS side)
doc.description: The NMOS output copy sinking K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is the other half of the output conductance.

rows.name: Gm_out
rows.note: output transconductance = mirror ratio times the input gm

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output node loaded by both output mirror devices' conductance

rows.name: Av
rows.note: DC gain; K_m scales Gm_out and (via the K_m-larger output devices) Rout inversely, so gain is nearly K_m-independent

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the input mirror-load density at the actual input gm

rows.name: vn_gbw
rows.note: estimate: input density if the pair were sized to just meet GBW_target at this K_m — grows as sqrt(K_m), the current-mirror OTA's noise-for-bandwidth trade

rows.name: f_pole
rows.note: estimate: the mirror-node pole, set by the diode gm over its own plus the K_m-scaled output gate cap

rules.note: estimate: keep the mirror-node pole well above GBW for phase margin; sim owns the real stability
the tail-node placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
the diode mirror's declared vds should equal its actual vgs; retune vgs_est_ml if this trips
